summary: You demonstrated strong architectural reasoning, especially in Question 2 where you effectively justified a modular monolith with scenario-specific trade-offs. To improve, focus on technical precision: ensure all quality attribute response measures are quantifiable, carry calculations through to end-to-end results, frame the CAP theorem accurately around partition tolerance, include negative trade-offs in ADRs and pattern analyses, and strictly adhere to word limits across all responses.
next_steps: In Question 1, replace subjective response measures with precise, quantifiable metrics such as explicit uptime percentages or recovery time objectives.
In Question 3(c), remember to multiply redundant subsystem availability back into the full series chain to calculate overall end-to-end system availability and downtime.
In Questions 4 and 6, consistently balance architectural recommendations by analyzing operational trade-offs, such as tuning parameters (e.g., trip thresholds) and negative consequences.

criteria.C1: You justified performance and availability well, providing a complete performance scenario. To reach Excellent, ensure your Question 1 availability response measure is objectively measurable rather than qualitative ('stay up most of the time'), fully completing all six scenario elements.
criteria.C2: Excellent work recommending a modular monolith. You effectively grounded your two trade-offs in CampusEats' specific constraints (team size and operational overhead) while explicitly acknowledging the downsides of shared-process failures.
criteria.C3: Parts (a) and (b) were calculated accurately with clear working. For Excellent, complete part (c) by multiplying the redundant payment provider's availability back into the series chain to find total end-to-end availability and downtime.
criteria.C4: You clearly explained the Circuit Breaker mechanism and effectively mapped it to the lunch outage. To achieve Excellent, discuss at least one operational drawback or tuning consideration, such as threshold limits or recovery timeouts.
criteria.C5: You selected sensible techniques like Redis and idempotency keys. To reach Excellent, apply the CAP theorem correctly: distributed systems cannot forfeit partition tolerance (P), meaning you must choose between consistency (CP) or availability (AP) during a partition.
criteria.C6: Your ADR successfully includes Context, Decision, and positive Consequences tailored to CampusEats. To attain Excellent, document negative consequences as well, such as added architectural complexity, queue maintenance overhead, or eventual consistency delays.
criteria.C7: Your formatting, terminology, and IEEE citations were handled well. To reach Excellent, ensure every response remains strictly within the 150-word limit; Question 2 currently exceeds this constraint at approximately 181 words.
